Prune for airflow and avoid wetting foliage when watering.

symptoms: Orange leaf spots may occur; confirm the host and nearby alternate hosts before treatment.
organic: Remove heavily affected fallen leaves and improve canopy airflow.
chemical: Use a locally registered rust fungicide only when a qualified adviser confirms it is warranted.
cedar_apple_rust.dosage: Follow the product label for apple, growth stage, pre-harvest interval, and local registration.
prevention: Choose resistant cultivars where available and use local guidance for alternate-host management.

symptoms: Dark fruit lesions or branch cankers may be consistent with black rot but need field confirmation.
organic: Prune cankered wood in dry weather and remove mummified fruit and infected debris.
chemical: A locally registered fungicide may be used only as part of an integrated, confirmed disease plan.
black_rot.dosage: Use the exact product label rate and observe protective equipment and pre-harvest restrictions.
prevention: Sanitize pruning tools, remove infected debris, and avoid wounding branches where practical.

symptoms: Target-like leaf spots can be associated with early blight; inspect the crop and lower leaves.
organic: Remove badly affected leaves, mulch to reduce soil splash, and water at the base.
chemical: If confirmed, consult local extension guidance for a registered product and resistance rotation.
early_blight.dosage: Use the exact label rate for the named crop and product; observe the re-entry and harvest intervals.
prevention: Rotate crops, remove volunteer hosts, maintain spacing, and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.

symptoms: Rapidly expanding dark lesions can be serious; this image result is not a confirmation.
organic: Isolate suspect plants where possible and remove diseased material without composting it.
chemical: Contact local agricultural extension promptly; only use locally registered products after confirmation.
late_blight.dosage: Follow the exact local product label. Do not apply a product based only on an image prediction.
prevention: Use clean seed or transplants, destroy volunteers, and monitor local disease alerts.
